R286.note: Sniffs bytes with http.DetectContentType, allowlists png/jpeg and discards the client filename for a random server-chosen name with a mapped extension; the MaxBytesReader and O_EXCL additions are stated and fit the contract (unstated 0o600 mode vs os.Create's 0666 is the only quiet change, and only matters if a different uid serves the files).

R287.note: RFC 4515 escaping of backslash, *, (, ) and NUL before the filter is built closes the injection and accepts any legitimate cn value; null now yields (cn=) instead of (cn=null), which is immaterial.

R288.note: Build FAIL: the write-up adds a second IChatMessageStore in a new file that collides with the one in ChatMessageStore.cs (CS0101), and even without the collision the new three-argument DeleteMessageAsync is never implemented on ChatMessageStore; the design (ownership-or-Moderator enforced in the store, false -> HubException) is sound but unbuildable, and deleting a nonexistent id now throws where it previously broadcast.

R289.note: Both fallback arguments now go through escapeshellarg; passing $source (basename under /srv/uploads) instead of the raw name is stated plainly and matches what the primary command already uses; return values and discarded output arrays preserved.

R290.note: PreparedStatement with setString on the same connection closes the injection; outputUpdateComplete now receives the placeholder text rather than the interpolated value, and the write-up states this.

R291.note: Straight Statement -> PreparedStatement conversion with a bound parameter; query, logging and finally cleanup unchanged.

R292.note: Pre-checking each member name with resolve()/is_relative_to closes ../ and absolute-path members, but linkname is never checked and resolve() cannot see a symlink the archive has not created yet, so a symlink member pointing outside followed by a member written through it still escapes workspace_dir under legacy extractall (the case filter='data' exists to close; it was backported to 3.11.4, not only 3.12+); legitimate bundles extract as before and the staged file is now removed on rejection.

R293.note: Replacing BinaryFormatter with System.Text.Json into Dictionary<string, JsonElement> is the correct fix since BinaryFormatter cannot be made safe, but every existing binary-serialized blob now fails to restore and the cached object changes type; the write-up states the wire-format break as a required producer-side follow-up, so 1 not 0.

R294.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode at the only HTML-emitting sink neutralizes element-content injection; encoded output is the only observable change and it is the fix.

R295.note: escapeshellarg closes the shell-metacharacter vector (and the hostname grammar also blocks a leading-dash option injection), but the added IP/RFC-1123 allowlist rejects values the original accepted and ping would resolve - underscored labels, trailing-dot FQDNs, IPv6 zone IDs - and reports them as reachable:false with a 200 rather than an error; the restriction is stated but no contract calls for it.

R296.note: Rejects CR/LF/NUL rather than stripping them and sends the mailbox as an RFC 3501 quoted string with backslash and double-quote escaped, so the value can only be the single SELECT argument; quoting a plain name like INBOX is accepted identically by servers, and names with spaces that previously broke now work.

R297.note: Passing an ldapjs EqualityFilter object as opts.filter keeps the value as a BER assertion value rather than filter text, so metacharacters cannot alter structure; the explanation's claim that escaping happens at wire-build time is imprecise (BER needs none) but the outcome is correct and legitimate lookups are unchanged.
